title: 215-16 Northern Boulevard: rear yard along the short dimension of the block (ZR 23-344(b), (c)(3))

question.text: Is a rear yard required on lot 70 (or on a zoning lot of lots 1 and 70) beyond the corner area, given ZR 23-344(b) and how the neighbouring lot lines are classified for 23-344(c)(3)?
question.property: 215-16 Northern Boulevard, Queens (borough 4, block 7334, lot 70; BBL 4073340070)

exceptions_considered: 23-344(a) is a point test (within 100 ft of the intersection of two street lines); it neither replaces nor defeats the street-line test of (b). The 144.60 ft GIS diagonal from the corner tests (a) only.
23-344(c) applies only to the portion of a side lot line beyond 100 ft of the street line it intersects.
23-344(d) applies if the confirmed layout has several rear lot lines.
The C2-2 overlay's residential/commercial rules (ZR 35-22, 35-50) were not read here.
A rear-yard exception waives no lot coverage, setback, window or open-space rule and no private right.

gap (c) ALLEY: a block is bounded only by #streets#, #public parks#, railroad rights-of-way at/above grade, airport boundaries, pierhead/shore lines, or NYC corporate boundary lines (12-10 'block', E10). A tax-map 'ALLEY' label (E6) is a Department of Finance notation, not one of those feature types unless the alley is itself a #street# (12-10 'street', E8: a way established on the City Map, or a qualifying public way); it does not by itself bound the block for the short-dimension measure.

gap (d) irregular blocks: 12-10 'short dimension of a block' (E2) measures 'the dimension between any two #streets# bounding the #block#'; 23-363(a) supplies an irregular-ANGLE rule for lot DEPTH only ('measured at the midpoint of such irregularly angled #lot line#'), not for a block frontage. No explicit method for choosing/measuring the frontage of a non-rectangular block was found (searches).

gap (e) district boundary: 23-344(c)(3) and (d)(3) as read key on the SUBJECT being R6 through R12 and on the ADJOINING lot's lot-line type (side vs rear), not on the adjoining zoning lot's district. Whether any 'Special Provisions Applying Along District Boundaries' changes the rear yard because the same-block neighbours are R4B was not confirmed from the primary source (searches).
meaning_and_applicability.reading: Block 7334's Northern Boulevard frontage between 215 Street and 215 Place measures 200.01 ft on the tax map and 203.13 ft in GIS; both are under 230 ft, so it is a short dimension of a block (E2). gap (b): the "short dimension of a block" is ONE determination of the block (block frontage < 230 ft between two #streets# bounding the #block#, E2/E10); the same fact is consumed by 23-344(b) (no rear yard within 100 ft of that street line, E1) AND by 23-363(c) (100 percent lot coverage within 100 ft of that street line, E11) - it is measured once, not twice, and never once per street name. Lots 1 and 70 front that frontage; under (b) no rear yard would be required within 100 ft of the Northern Boulevard street line, which covers the lot. gap (a): how far the lot reaches from that line is in conflict - 100 ft (tax-map depth label, printed_tax_map), 99.97 ft (GIS, measured to the lot's own frontage edge) and about 101.06 ft (derived, measured to the mapped street line taken as the centreline offset by half the mapped width); no basis is chosen here, so whether the far edge lies within or beyond 100 ft of the operative street line is left for a survey or the approved ZD1. Lots 11 and 61 front 215 Place and 215 Street; their north lines are neither front nor rear lines of those lots, so they are side lot lines (E3, E4), and under (c)(3) (R6 to R12) no rear yard would be required where the subject's rear lot line coincides with them. gap (e): those neighbouring lots are in R4B (PLUTO), but 23-344(c)(3) keys on the subject R6B district and the neighbour's lot-line type, not the neighbour's district. A labelled draft reading, not a DOB determination.

PLUTO LotFront reports only one frontage on a corner lot (E14) and must never be used as the block frontage for the short-dimension measure; the short dimension of a block is a single measurement consumed by both 23-344(b) and 23-363(c) (never added twice).

observed_facts: ZR 12-10: the short dimension of a block is a block frontage where the dimension between any two bounding streets measures less than 230 feet.
ZR 12-10 'block' (E10): a block is bounded only by #streets#, #public parks#, railroad rights-of-way at or above grade, airport boundaries, pierhead/shore lines, or NYC corporate boundary lines.

ZR 12-10 'street' (E8) and 'street setback line' (E9) are both defined terms; a #street setback line# exists only on the City Map in Staten Island or Queens Community District 10 and, where it exists, supersedes the #street line# for yard/height/setback/court rules.
ZR 23-344(b): no rear yard is required within 100 feet of the street line of the short dimension of a block where a front lot line of a zoning lot coincides with it.
ZR 23-363(c): within 100 feet of the street line of the short dimension of a block, the maximum lot coverage is 100 percent - the same short-dimension-of-a-block test as 23-344(b).
Tax map (2017, 2021): lot 70 100.76 by 100 ft and lot 1 99.25 by 100 ft; frontages sum to 200.01 ft; an 'ALLEY' label runs across the southern part of the northern lots.

GIS: combined frontage 203.12900 ft; lot 70's maximum distance from the Northern line 99.97460 ft; the independent hand calculation derives about 101.06 ft from the Northern Boulevard street line to the lot's far edge (line 97, under the line-offset assumption at line 92).

PLUTO data dictionary (E14): LotFront is the tax lot's frontage in feet and, where a lot fronts more than one street, the side is often set by the PTS building address; LotDepth is the tax lot's depth in feet; DOF computes LotArea as LotFront x LotDepth for a regular lot and from the Digital Tax Map for an irregular lot.
PLUTO: every other lot on block 7334 (the 215 Place and 215 Street frontages) is zoned R4B; the subject lots 1 and 70 are R6B with a C2-2 overlay.
conclusion.interpretation: Conditional no-rear-yard reading under 23-344(b), with 23-344(c)(3) as an alternative along the neighbours' side lot lines; awaiting independent review; not a DOB determination.
conflicts: Block frontage 200.01 ft (tax map) against 203.13 ft (GIS): both under 230 ft, so the same outcome.

The three differ by about 1 ft, which straddles the 100 ft line in 23-344(b); no basis is chosen - a survey or the approved ZD1 settles it.

The neighbours' tax-lot lines must also be their zoning-lot lines (never equate a tax lot with a zoning lot).
The operative street line and depth come from a survey or the approved ZD1.
